why: One ceiling per theme and surface, in bytes of inlined CSS and tagged JS. A page at or under its ceiling is the theme as it ships; a page above it is a rule that arrived from another surface. A lower number records an improvement, a higher one is a decision that shows in the diff. Byte counts are read from the built bundle under public/dist, so a tree without a build is not measured here.

decisions.ohniva: 2026-11-28: 36928 -> 47455 bytes. The IE6 sheet is 4245 bytes and is inlined for every reader, because the kernel owns <head> and cannot wrap the file in a conditional comment; every rule is scoped under .oh-ie6, so a modern browser downloads it and matches nothing. The other 6282 bytes are the template's rail, four banners, gallery, the four @font-face blocks and the fixed backdrop. The backdrop veil adds 605 bytes (47455 -> 48060): the translucent layer, the two repeating grid gradients and the top gradient. The four colour washes add 354 bytes (48060 -> 48414): four radial gradients in cyan, gold, orange and blue at 16 to 26 percent alpha, under the grid, so the wash is irregular without turning the header unreadable.
